cards.explanation: The answer is go fishing. Simon Peter says it plain: "I am going fishing." (John 21:3) And the others answer, "We will go with you…" and off they go to the boat. I'd love to have friends who say yes like that when I say I'm heading out.

The answer is nothing. The text says they "…caught nothing that night." (John 21:3) That's a whole night of work with an empty net to show for it. I think that boat had some quiet morning faces on it.

The answer is that He asks if they have any fish. He calls out, "Children, do you have any fish?" (John 21:5) Simple question, and the answer is a short one: "No." Notice the disciples still don't know who's asking (John 21:4). A stranger on the shore, a question about the catch, and the whole morning is about to change.

The answer is True, friends. The disciples say they have no fish, and the Man on the shore says, "Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some." (John 21:6) Short instruction, big result. I think it's something to see that they do it, since they still don't know who He is (John 21:4).

The answer is that they can't haul it in with so many fish. They cast the net where He said, and they "…were unable to haul it in because of the great number of fish." (John 21:6) Empty all night, then too full to lift. That's a whole new problem, and a good one to have.
The answer is the disciple Jesus loved, friends. He speaks up and tells Peter, "It is the Lord!" (John 21:7) The text doesn't name him here, so I won't either.

The answer is False. Peter doesn't stay in the boat. The text says he "…put on his outer garment (for he had removed it) and jumped into the sea." (John 21:7) He hears "It is the Lord!" and moves, no waiting around.

The answer is False. The text says they were "…not far from land, only about a hundred yards." (John 21:8) That's a short trip, not a mile. The others bring the boat in and drag the net of fish ashore.

The answer is False. Even with fish already on the fire (John 21:9), Jesus says, "Bring some of the fish you have just caught." (John 21:10) He doesn't tell them to sit it out. He asks them to bring some of their own catch.
The answer is 153, friends. The text says the net "…was full of large fish, 153…" (John 21:11) Somebody counted those fish. I get that, because I'd count my cookies too.
The answer is torn. The text says, "…even with so many, the net was not torn." (John 21:11) 153 large fish is a lot of weight for one net. The text makes a point of telling us it held.

The answer is Jesus Himself, friends. The text says, "Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish." (John 21:13) He called them to breakfast, and then He's the one who serves them. I think that's a pretty humble way to start a morning.

The answer is third, friends. The text says, "This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead." (John 21:14) So this isn't the first time they've seen Him. The word "now" tells us it's one more appearance added to the ones before.
